title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 53 (Prohibition on Issue of Shares at a Discount)

content.overview: Section 53 prohibits a company from issuing shares at a discount. Any share issued by a company at a discounted price is void. Exception is made for sweat equity shares issued in accordance with section 54. Contravention attracts liability to pay the amount received with interest at a prescribed rate and penalties.
content.glance: No issue of shares at a discount; discounted issue is void; sweat equity under s. 54 is the main exception; refund with interest and penalties on breach.
content.study: Except as provided in section 54, a company shall not issue shares at a discount. Any share issued by a company at a discounted price shall be void. Where a company contravenes this section, the company shall be liable to pay to the person who received the shares the amount of the consideration received, with interest at a rate not less than the rate prescribed, and the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty. Current-law framing: identify proposed or actual issue price below nominal value; apply the prohibition unless s. 54 sweat equity applies; state voidness and refund/penalty consequences.

sections.heading: Prohibition
sections.body: A company shall not issue shares at a discount, except as provided in section 54 (sweat equity).

sections.heading: Voidness
sections.body: Any share issued at a discounted price is void.

sections.heading: Consequences
sections.body: Company must pay the consideration received with prescribed interest; company and officers in default face penalties.

provisions.title: Prohibition on issue of shares at a discount

examples.title: Discounted issue void
examples.body: A company issues ₹10 face-value shares at ₹8. The issue is void under s. 53; consideration must be returned with interest.

examples.title: Sweat equity exception
examples.body: Shares issued as sweat equity under s. 54 in accordance with that section fall outside the s. 53 prohibition.

hypotheticals.question: Can a company issue shares below par to attract investors?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 53 prohibits issue at a discount; such issue is void, subject to the sweat equity exception under s. 54.

distinctions.title: Discount prohibition (s. 53) vs sweat equity (s. 54)
distinctions.right: Permitted issue of sweat equity on prescribed conditions

misconceptions.trap: Any below-par issue can be validated by shareholder approval alone.
misconceptions.correction: Section 53 makes discounted issues void, subject only to the statutory sweat equity route under s. 54.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 53 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Compare issue price to nominal value. II. Apply prohibition unless s. 54. III. State voidness and refund/penalty. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Issue terms; discount analysis; s. 54 if claimed; consequences; precise relief.
